match.reason: None of the bank points teaches that each text builds its own world of places, people, time and values for readers to enter; the closest, context of reception, is about how readers' values shape interpretation rather than the world a text constructs, so it is a related but different idea.

draft.title: The world of a text
card: Every text builds its own world. It is made from the places, people, time and values that the writer chooses to show.
Setting is the place and time. A story set in a fishing town in the 1950s has different limits and chances from one set in a city today.
Values are what the people in that world treat as right, normal or important. A text can show them through what characters praise, fear or punish.
Readers enter this world as they read. They can understand its rules and values even when they differ from their own.
draft.remember: A text's world is made of its places, people, time and values, and readers learn its rules as they read.

a.q: Which sentence best describes the world of a text?
opts: The places, people, time and values the writer builds
The real events that happened when the author was alive
The opinion a reader forms after finishing the text
The list of techniques the writer uses in each paragraph
a.why: A text's world is what the writer builds from setting, people, time and values. A reader's opinion comes after entering that world, and a list of techniques describes how it is built, not the world itself.
a.clue: Think of what a writer creates for the reader to step into.

b.q: In a novel, a village punishes anyone who leaves the family farm. Neil, a teenager, is shamed for wanting to study in the city. What does this show about the world of the text?
opts: It values staying loyal to family and place
It values education above all other goals
It shows that Neil is a careless person
It shows that the village is a modern city
b.why: The village punishes leaving, so its values favour loyalty to family and place. Neil's wish to study shows a different want, but the village's reaction, not Neil's wish, shows the values of that world.
b.clue: Look at how the village reacts, not at what Neil wants.

a.best: The places, people, time and values the writer builds

b.best: It values staying loyal to family and place
